A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching title, authors, and research scope. All 21 pages of each version, including Appendices A–H, are readable; text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulated and real-device experiments on synthetic data and QM9 in Tables I–IV, plus original image-generation, flow-matching, and negative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their outcomes, including the main benchmarking tables and the supplementary results in Appendices C–H.

M1.justification: The latent samplers, modified MolGAN architecture, training procedures, DDGAN integration, and flow-matching decoder remain unchanged. Section IV expands the explanation of existing photonic samples without introducing a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-mixture, synthetic quantum, Bernoulli, QM9, CIFAR-10, and moons datasets and tasks. The negative experiments highlighted in v3's discussion were already present in v2's Appendix H.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including the photonic, Bernoulli, and Gaussian latents in the main benchmarks. Normalizing flows are newly discussed as possible trained priors but are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: The reported experimental settings and metrics remain unchanged, including latent dimensions, circuit configurations, training budgets, and QM9's 10,000 generation attempts. The added metric labels in Section IV.B do not change their definitions; Appendix H retains its existing alternative training regime.

E4.justification: The circuit-architecture comparisons, real-versus-simulated device comparison, training curves, generated examples, and training-sensitivity experiments are retained. Section V adds discussion of existing negative results, not a new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Run counts and uncertainty reporting are unchanged: Table I uses 12 runs, the QM9 comparisons report standard errors over 20 seeds, and the DDGAN and StyleGAN tables use five seeds. Circuit-randomization exceptions and Figure 4's uncertainty reporting also remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables I–VIII retain identical entries and numerical values, and the result figures are unchanged. For example, size-16 quantum QM9 FCD remains 1.160 ± 0.06, and quantum DDGAN FID remains 4.025 ± 0.075. The added qualifications concern interpretation of existing findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, GAN-induced distance, Remark 1, Theorem 1, Corollary 1, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. The correction from reconstructing inputs 'from the inputs' to 'from the outputs' repairs wording in the inversion example without revising the mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims: conditional preservation of nonclassical sampling complexity, proposed mechanisms for practical benefits, and benchmarking advantages on selected datasets. The new qualifications do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Sections III.D–IV explicitly distinguish a matched structured prior from computational separation, describe QM9's quantum origin as a heuristic, and qualify cross-dataset L1 comparisons because supports differ. v3 also explains potential confounding from trained priors and connects the existing negative results to its applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Section IV adds photon-count vector examples and explicitly describes constructing distinguishable-photon samples by summing independently routed single-photon outcomes. This documents the existing sampler more clearly; implementation links, hyperparameters, hardware, and timing information are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds 'Stochastic interpolants: A unifying framework for flows and diffusions' as reference 54 to support its discussion of flexible source distributions. Other reference changes mainly update publication metadata for existing works; the central positioning against prior quantum-latent research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized paragraph expansions in Sections III.D, IV, and V, grammar corrections, clearer metric terminology, and bibliographic editing. The main section order and Appendices A–H remain intact, with almost no appendix rewriting.

P2.justification: Added prose causes limited layout changes: Table I moves from page 6 to page 7, other main-text tables shift vertically, and the conclusion moves to page 10. All seven figures and eight tables retain their designs, captions, and displayed content.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the calibration of the existing evidence by qualifying QM9's theoretical relevance and cross-dataset distance comparisons, and by explaining how the retained negative results limit applicability. The clearer sampler description also helps readers assess the controls. These are useful, limited improvements to an otherwise unchanged empirical and theoretical contribution.
